_comment: The multi-site survey, as RMF tasks.
What separates this from warehouse_xl_survey.json is that every action
now takes a site, so no action has a fixed destination any more. The
bridge resolves a destination from the argument named by waypoint_arg,
translates it through the zones table, and pins the task to the robot the
planner's agent is bound to. Two robots therefore go to two different
places under one action name, which is what the multi-site policy asks
for and what the single-site map could not express.
The zones table is an identity here because the domain's site names were
chosen to be the waypoints' pinned names. It is written out rather than
omitted because the two are different things that happen to agree: one is
an object in an EPDDL problem, the other a vertex in a navigation graph,
and the day a site moves this is the line that moves it.
outcomes is the simulator's ground truth and is consulted only when the
perception node has said nothing. The launch file writes it from the same
argument that places the pallet, so the fallback cannot disagree with the
world the robots are actually driving through.
